deep.reconstruction:
Notation (Gauss): P(x)=Σ_{n∈Z} x^{n²} and P(x,y)=Σ x^{n²}y^n. pt := P(e^{-πt}) = θ3(q) with q=e^{-πt}. p(t,u) := P(e^{-πt},e^{2πu}). In the AGM part, pM is the same function of M, with q=e^{-Mπ}, and τ = iM.

(0) Top line. p' = π^{1/4}/Π(-1/4) is the special value p(1) = θ3(e^{-π}) = π^{1/4}/Γ(3/4) ≈ 1.0864348. The second form follows from the reflection formula Γ(1/4)Γ(3/4)=π√2 and Π(1/4)=Γ(5/4)=Γ(1/4)/4. It gives p' = Π(1/4)(4/π)^{3/4} exactly. Hence the trailing '/4' (struck-looking in the image) must not be there.

(1) AGM / modular invariance. Gauss's setting: m = μ·θ3(q)² and n = μ·θ4(q)², with q=e^{-Mπ} and μ = M(m,n). Then n/m = θ4²/θ3² (the complementary modulus k'). Claim: M may be replaced by either of two expressions.
- The finite continued fraction 1/(2ai+1/(2bi+…+1/(2ei+1/M))), with an odd number of integers a,b,…,e.
- Equivalently, the Möbius map M ↦ (pM+2qi)/(r+2sMi) with pr+4qs=1.
Gauss also rationalises this to the form [M+2(qr-psMM)i]/(rr+4ssMM). That form is the correct identity for real M, i.e. the real/imaginary split.
In τ=iM the map is τ ↦ (pτ-2q)/(2sτ+r), a matrix of the principal congruence group Γ(2). In the continued fraction, M ↦ 1/M is S and M ↦ M+2ki is T^{-2k}. An odd number of partial quotients gives an even number of S's, hence again Γ(2). So the two descriptions agree.

(2) Right-hand chain (theta multiplier via continuants). Put M' = 2ei+1/M, M'' = 2di+1/M', …, M^V = 2ai+1/M^IV.
- Since e^{-2πik n²}=1 and p(1/M)=√M·pM, each step gives pM^{(k+1)} = √M^{(k)}·pM^{(k)}.
- Hence pM^V = √(M M' M'' M''' M^IV)·pM.
- The product telescopes to Gauss's continuant bracket (Disq. Arith. art. 27): M M' ⋯ M^IV = [2bi,2ci,2di,2ei,M]. For example M M' = 2eiM+1 = [2ei,M].

(3) Boxed note. It reads '= M* | √M·pM = √M*·pM* (ungerade); √M·pM = pM*/√M* (gerade)', with a wavy line marking alternation; M* is the continued fraction value. The odd case checks for a single partial quotient: M* = 1/(2ai+1/M) gives √M*·pM* = √M·pM.

(4) Basic properties of pt.
- p(t+2ik) = pt.
- pt = t^{-1/2}·p(1/t), Jacobi's imaginary transformation.
- Two-variable version: e^{-uu/(4πt)}·√t·p(t,u) = p(1/t, iu/t). By Poisson summation the exponent u²/(4πt) is right if y=e^{u}. With y=e^{2πu} as written it must be πu²/t.

(5) Jacobi-type identities. Here p(t+i)=θ4, p(t/4)=θ3+θ2 and p(t/4+i)=θ3-θ2.
- pt⁴ = p(t+i)⁴ + (½p(t/4) - ½p(t/4+i))⁴, i.e. θ3⁴ = θ4⁴ + θ2⁴.
- pt = ½p(t/4) + ½p(t/4+i).
- pt + p(t+i) = 2p(4t), i.e. θ3(q)+θ4(q) = 2θ3(q⁴).
- Hence p(t+i) = 2p(4t) - pt = t^{-1/2}(p(1/(4t)) - p(1/t)). This is θ4(e^{-πt}) = t^{-1/2}θ2(e^{-π/t}).

(6) Quadratic-exponent sums. With h=e^{-π}: Σ h^{αnn+2βn+γ} = h^{γ-ββ/α}/√α · Σ h^{nn/α + 2βi n/α}. This is (4) with t=α, u=-β. It is the theoretical basis of the previous page's 'summation of a series whose logarithms form a 2nd-order arithmetic progression' (α' = a + bb/4c + …, β' = i·180°·b/c, γ' = k²π²/c).

Purpose: the transformation theory of θ3, θ4 and of the modulus k' under the modular group. This describes all M (the multivalued AGM) with the same n/m. It leads into the next page's reduction of pM, qM, rM via binary quadratic forms.
errors: The invariance of n/m=θ4²/θ3² is stated for all p,q,r,s with pr+4qs=1, i.e. all of Γ(2). Strictly, k'=θ4²/θ3² changes sign under Γ(2) elements whose lower-left entry 2s ≡ 2 mod 4: under τ→τ+2, θ2²→-θ2², and S T^{±2} S sends k'→-k'. So the equality holds exactly only when s is even. In general it holds up to sign: k'² is Γ(2)-invariant, and a sign change of n is absorbed by the multivaluedness of the AGM. Gauss's statement as written is imprecise.
Top line: the second expression is correct as Π(1/4)(4/π)^{3/4}. The extra division by 4 (if intended) would make it wrong by a factor 4.
The factor e^{-uu/(4πt)} is consistent with p(t,u)=P(e^{-πt}, e^{u}). With the written P(e^{-πt}, e^{2πu}) the correct factor is e^{-πuu/t}. Either a convention slip or a misreading of the exponent.

Boxed relations √M·pM = √M*·pM* ('ungerade') and √M·pM = pM*/√M* ('gerade'): only the one-step odd case could be verified. For longer chains the correct multiplier is the continuant product given in the right column, so the box is at best a special-case note.
